newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIUM UNIONS SHOULD FOLLOW DUTCH LEAD - CEN.BANK.
newsitem.headline: BELGIUM UNIONS SHOULD FOLLOW DUTCH LEAD - CEN.BANK.

text.p: Belgian labour unions should follow the example of their Dutch neighbours and focus on job creation rather than wage rises, the Belgian central bank said.
"Ten years ago Dutch unions and employers' organisations agreed to put the priority on job creation, not wage increases.
Belgium did the opposite, and look at the result," governor Alfons Verplaetse said at the presentation of the bank's annual report on Wednesday.
His comments were embargoed for Friday.
At the end of 1996 9.4 percent of Belgium's civilian labour force was unemployed compared to just 6.4 percent in the Netherlands.
"The single most important problem Belgium is facing today is unemployment. We need a contract between unions and employers to put job creation at the top of the agenda," Verplaetse said.
Wage restraint and job sharing were the keys to creating more jobs. Reducing the cost of labour would boost the job-creating effect of economic growth, he said.
Unions and employers last year failed to agree a deal on jobs and wages, forcing the government to impose wage curbs.
Verplaetse said that he would personally try to rebuild confidence between unions and employers, whose organisations are represented on the Regents Council of the central bank.
"We need to decide what the priority is: increase the wages of those who have jobs, or create jobs for those who have none," he said in a rare emotional appeal.
